rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خزنة means keepers of a store; the word here rebukes and reproaches the people in painful humiliation.
rows.anchor: تقريعا وتوبيخا في الإيلام والتوجيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers are the angels appointed to guard Hell and punish its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: حفظة جهنم وزبانيتها وهم : الملائكة الموكلون بتعذيب أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers were humans of the addressees’ own kind, making it easier to consult them and understand their speech.
rows.anchor: من جنسكم آدميون مثلكم ليسهل عليكم مراجعتهم وفهم كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs are what He revealed to the prophets.
rows.anchor: وهو ما أنزل الله على الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers warned them by frightening them with the consequences.
rows.anchor:
يخوفونكم.
{لقآء يومكم هاذا} ؛ أي : وقتكم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This means the time of entering Hell, not the Resurrection Day: ‘day’ is commonly used for a time of distress, and the Resurrection is not exclusive to disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقت دخولهم النار لا يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reproach grounds accountability in messengers’ arrival and delivery of scripture, evidence that there is no obligation before revealed law.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه لا تكليف قبل الشرع من حيث أنهم عللوا توبيخهم بإتيان الرسل وتبليغ الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit the messengers came, recited, and warned them, but their admission comes when confession can no longer benefit them.
rows.anchor: وأنذرونا فأقروا في وقت لا ينفعهم الإقرار والاعتراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The binding sentence of punishment is God’s declaration to Iblis that He will fill Hell with him and his followers.
rows.anchor: لاملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They explain that they were among Iblis’s followers: they denied the messengers and claimed God had sent nothing.
rows.anchor: وقد كنا ممن تبع إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker of the command is left unspecified to make the utterance more terrifying; their entry is understood as an eternal one.
rows.anchor: مقدرا خلودكم فيها وإبهام القائل لتهويل المقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine wisdom creates Hell and its people to manifest the attribute of subduing severity, just as it creates Paradise and its people to manifest gentleness; the primordial decree sends them into Hell by force.
rows.anchor: إظهارا لصفة القهر أن يخلق النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell’s seven gates signify seven blameworthy traits; the damned remain trapped in them, unable to change them as the godfearing can leave such traits behind.
rows.anchor: وهي الصفات الذميمة السبع التي مر ذكرها خالدين فيها بحيث لا يمكن الخروج من هذه الصفات الذميمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذَروني means ‘leave me alone’; Bursevī cites the lexicon’s note that the verb’s past, verbal noun, and active participle are not used.
rows.anchor: خلوا عني واتركوني يقال : ذره ؛ أي : دعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claims that killing Moses is necessary for his rule; his courtiers repeatedly restrain him, calling Moses weak and only a magician.
rows.anchor: فإني أعلم أن صلاح ملكي في قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The courtiers warn that killing Moses would make people suspect Pharaoh had failed to answer his proof and resorted to the sword.
rows.anchor: إذا قتلته أدخلت على الناس شبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh pretends his courtiers alone keep him from killing Moses, but what actually restrains him is his overwhelming private fear.
rows.anchor: وما كان الذي يكفه إلا ما في نفسه من الفزع الهائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh was convinced Moses was a prophet, yet feared that killing him would bring immediate destruction.
rows.anchor: ولكن كان يخاف إن هم بقتله أن يعاجل بالهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh taunts Moses to call on the Lord he claims sent him to protect him; Pharaoh outwardly fears Moses and inwardly fears his prayer.
rows.anchor: وهو يخاف منه ظاهرا ويخاف من دعاء ربه باطنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing their religion means replacing their worship of Pharaoh and idols, which they worship as a means of drawing near to God.
rows.anchor: بغير ما أنتم عليه من الدين الذي هو عبارة عن عبادته وعبادة الأصنام لتقربهم إليه

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Moses cannot change their religion entirely, Pharaoh alleges he may bring worldly disorder through conflict and violence; ‘or’ offers either alternative.
rows.anchor: ما يفسد دنياكم من التحارب والتهارج إن لم يقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blind-hearted Pharaoh imagines God or his people will let him kill Moses, not realizing God will destroy him and his people and save Moses and his people.
rows.anchor: ظن أن الله يذره أن يقتل موسى بحوله وقوته أو يذره قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh fears a change of religion and earthly disorder, but not the destruction of himself and his people or the ruin of their condition in both worlds.
rows.anchor: ولم يخاف هلاك نفسه وهلاك قومه وفساد حالهم في الدارين

words: إِنِّى عُذْتُ بِرَبِّى وَرَبِّكُم مِّن كُلِّ مُتَكَبِّرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the overpowering one above all, as stated in the verse about His being dominant over them.
rows.anchor: فالقاهر فوق الكل هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride is among the strongest traits of the commanding self and must therefore be removed.
rows.anchor: من أشد صفات النفس الأمارة

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Jāmī’s poem teaches that removing pride from within is harder than uprooting a mountain with a needle, so one should not boast of humility.
rows.anchor:
قال المولى الجامي :
جزء : 8 رقم الصفحة : 148

words: وَقَالَ رَجُلٌۭ مُّؤْمِنٌۭ مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the plot to kill Moses spread, his friends grieved and his enemies rejoiced; God protected him and raised an outsider to calm the crisis and defend him.
rows.anchor: فلا جرم صانه الله من كل بلية وأوصله إلى كل أمنية

words: مُّؤْمِنٌۭ مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَٰنَهُۥٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مؤمن is the first of three descriptions of the man because it is noblest; من آل فرعون comes before يكتم إيمانه to prevent misreading it as the man’s relative clause.
rows.anchor: صفة ثالثة قدم الأول أعني مؤمن لكونه أشرف الأوصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person’s آل are those whose affairs return to him through kinship, companionship, or agreement in religion.
rows.anchor: وآل الرجل خاصته الذين يؤول إليه أمرهم للقرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer was a relative, specifically a cousin, of Pharaoh and the same person who had warned Moses of the plot in 28:20; Bursevī considers Shamaʿān the soundest reported name.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك الرجل المؤمن من أقارب فرعون

rows.speaker: الإمام السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhaylī identifies the believer as Shamaʿān and Bursevī calls this the soundest view.
rows.anchor: وهو أصح ما قيل فيه. قاله الإمام السهيلي

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī’s History gives the believer’s name as Jabr.
rows.anchor: وفي "تاريخ الطبري" : اسمه جبر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another identification is Ḥabīb al-Najjār, said to have made the chest in which Moses’s mother placed him in the river; he is distinguished from the man of Yā Sīn.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي عمل تابوت موسى حين أرادت أمه أن تلقيه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Other reported names for the believer are Khirbil ibn Nūḥāʾīl and Ḥizqīl.
rows.anchor: وقيل : خربيل بن نوحائيل أو حزقيل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report counts Ḥizqīl, the believer among Pharaoh’s people, Ḥabīb al-Najjār of Yā Sīn, and ʿAlī as three who never disbelieved; it says ʿAlī is best among them.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام سباق الأمم ثلاثة لم يكفروا بالله طرفة عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قوم is a vocative meaning ‘my people’; ملك means sovereignty, and ظاهرين describes them as currently dominant over the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: غالبين عالين على بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اليوم is connected to لكم, while ظاهرين is a circumstantial accusative describing the people.
rows.anchor: في قوله : اليوم ما تعلق به لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land means Egypt, where no one could oppose them at that time.
rows.anchor: أرض مصر لا يقاومكم أحد في هذا الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تحاجّ means mutual disputation, like محاجة; the Prophet is told to recall the time Hell’s inhabitants quarrel there.
rows.anchor: واذكر يا محمد لقومك وقت تخاصم أهل النار في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputants may be Pharaoh’s people or other inhabitants of Hell.
rows.anchor: سواء كانوا آل فرعون ، أو غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak are those of lower rank, standing, and worldly circumstances, glossed as servants and clients.
rows.anchor: منهم في القدر والمنزلة والحال في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كل is the subject, meaning ‘all of us—you and us’; فيها is its predicate, ‘in the Fire’.
rows.anchor: أي : كلنا نحن وأنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant cannot relieve the weak, since they too are in Hell and, even if able, would first relieve themselves.
rows.anchor: ولو قدرنا لأغنينا عن أنفسنا

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ حَكَمَ بَيْنَ ٱلْعِبَادِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has assigned each person’s outcome: believers enter Paradise at differing ranks and disbelievers Hell at differing levels, and none can overturn His judgment.
rows.anchor: فأدخل المؤمنين الجنة على تفاوتهم في الدرجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who ask the keepers include both the weak and the arrogant, after they have tasted the punishment and exhausted their options.
rows.anchor: جميعا ، لما ذاقوا شدة العذاب وضاقت حيلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers are those who administer punishment to Hell’s inhabitants.
rows.anchor: القوام بتعذيب أهل النار. جمع خازن

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib explains that خزن is to preserve something in a store, then by extension any kind of keeping, such as keeping a secret.
rows.anchor: قاله الراغب : ووضع جهنم موضع الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming Jahannam instead of using a pronoun heightens dread and horror; Jahannam is the name of God’s kindled fire.
rows.anchor: ووضع جهنم موضع الضمير للتهويل والتفظيع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask the keepers to intercede for them.
rows.anchor:
شافعين لنا.
{يخفف عنا يوما} ؛ أي : في مقدار يوم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for some reduction in punishment for the span of one earthly day.
rows.anchor: في مقدار يوم واحد من أيام الدنيا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوما is an adverb of duration for يخفف; its object is omitted, with من العذاب explaining that omitted object.
rows.anchor:
مفعوله محذوف.
ومن العذاب بيان لذلك المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They request only slight relief for a short time, rather than no punishment or a greater reduction for longer, because they know those larger requests are impossible.
rows.anchor: واقتصارهم في الاستدعاء على تخفيف قدر يسير من العذاب في مقدار قصير من الزمان دون رفعه رأسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers answer only after a delay.
rows.anchor: قالوا} : أي الخزنة بعد مدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza is interrogative and the waw coordinates the question with the omitted sense ‘did you not take notice of this’; the messengers’ coming is described as continual in worldly life.
rows.anchor: الهمزة للاستفهام ، والواو للعطف على مقداري ألم تنبهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers brought clear proofs of the evil end of disbelief and sins, to establish the damned’s guilt and reproach them for wasting the chance to pray and disabling its means of acceptance.
rows.anchor: بالحجج الواضحة الدالة على سوء عاقبة ما كنتم عليه من الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit that the messengers brought proofs, but say they rejected them, as in Sūrat al-Mulk.
rows.anchor: فكذبناهم كما في سورة الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers tell them to pray themselves because it would be implausible for the keepers to do it for them; the command is meant to extinguish hope and expose the truth, not promise an answer.
rows.anchor: ولم يريدوا بأمرهم بالدعاء أطماعهم في الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive can make الدعاء the disbelievers’ own prayer, or the prayer of others offered on their behalf.
rows.anchor: فالمصدر مضاف إلى فاعله ، أو وما دعاء غيرهم لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer is futile and void of effect because they make it at the wrong time.
rows.anchor: في ضياع وبطلان الإيجاب ؛ لأنهم دعوا في غير وقته

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority forbids saying that a disbeliever’s prayer is answered, citing this verse and arguing that disbelief means the person does not know God or has invalidated belief by describing Him improperly.
rows.anchor: يستجاب دعاء الكافرين ، فمنعه الجمهور

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some allow that a wronged person’s prayer is answered even if the person is a disbeliever, interpreting kufr here as ingratitude; Satan’s prayer for respite, which was granted, is also evidence, and Bursevī says the permissive ruling is followed.
rows.anchor: فمحمول على كفران النعمة وجوزه بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī also adduces God granting Satan’s request for respite as evidence that a disbeliever’s prayer can be answered.
rows.anchor: فقال الله تعالى : إنك من المنظرين

rows.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī’s poem illustrates the futility of idolatry: after an idol fails its devotee for years, God grants the need when the desperate man collapses at the temple.
rows.anchor:
قال الشيخ سعدي :
مغى در بروى از جهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining creation’s determination, the passage explains how it was brought about; attention to the earth and human livelihood first invites the addressees to faith and restrains disbelief and transgression.
rows.anchor: شروع في بيان كيفية التكوين إثر بيان كيفية التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم marks the ordered transition to the next stage and also signals special care in originating the higher realms.
rows.anchor: وفي ثم إظهار كمال العناية بإبداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though استوى ordinarily means becoming straight and even, it means to intend and turn toward here, since its bodily literal sense cannot apply to God.
rows.anchor: والاستواء ضد الاعوجاج من قولهم استوى العود إذا اعتدل واستقام حمل في هذا المقام على معنى القصد والتوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directed His will toward the heaven in a straight, undivided intention, without intending another creation comparable to it.
rows.anchor: ثم قصد نحو السماء بإرادته ومشيئته قصدا سويا وتوجه إليه توجها لا يلوي على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw is circumstantial and its feminine pronoun refers to the heaven; دخان is smoke, described as fine terrestrial particles lifted by heat.
rows.anchor: الواو للحال ، والضمير إلى السماء

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib’s lexicon describes smoke as smoke accompanying flame, and vapor as moist water-particles rising in air with rays reflected from water surfaces.
rows.anchor: الدخان العثان المستصحب للهب والبخار أجزاء مائية رطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heaven was a dark, smoke-like substance; calling it heaven anticipates its eventual state, and the comparison indicates it had no cohesion.
rows.anchor: أمر ظلماني يعد كالدخان ، وهو المرتفع من النار

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib reads ‘it is like smoke’ as indicating that the early heaven had no solidity.
rows.anchor: الراغب قوله تعالى : {وهي دخان}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Smoke’ may denote the heaven’s matter and bodily form or its minute constituent parts; their darkness was the obscurity before illumination, and their scattered, unconnected state resembled smoke.
rows.anchor: عبر بالدخان عن مادة السماء يعني : الهيولى والصورة الجسمية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view is that the heaven was vapor rising from water, shaped like smoke, as in al-Kāshifī’s commentary.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : وهي دخان

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: In a report answering Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq, Ibn ʿAbbās says the Throne was first created over water; fire made the water cast up froth for the earth, and its vapor became heaven before the earth was spread, its mountains fixed, and provisions, plants, animals, and rivers made.
rows.anchor: هذا جواب عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما لنافع بن الأزرق الحروري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation account distinguishes the earth’s initial creation from its later spreading and the subsequent setting of mountains and provision, citing ‘the earth after that He spread out.’
rows.anchor: بعد خلق السماء لذلك قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to heaven; the earth is the one whose existence and contents had been determined.
rows.anchor: فقال لها} : أي للسماء ، {وللأرض} التي قدر وجودها ووجود ما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means ‘come into being’: each realm is to exist in its appointed form and at its appointed time.
rows.anchor: كونا واحدثا على وجه معين ، وفي وقت مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command represents God’s effective will bringing heaven and earth into existence after their determination; there was no literal commander or commanded, only an analogy to an obeyed command.
rows.anchor: من غير أن يكون هناك آمر ومأمور كما في قوله : كن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طوعا and كرها are verbal nouns functioning as circumstantial expressions: willingly or unwillingly.
rows.anchor: مصدران واقعان في موقع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether they wished it or not, the image signifies that God’s power must take effect and cannot be resisted; it does not attribute rational will or choice to inanimate heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: وهو تمثيل لتحتم تأثير قدرته تعالى فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Among His signs’ means signs of God’s power.
rows.anchor: ومن ءاياته} : (وازنشانهاى قدرت الهيست)

rows.speaker: الإمام المرزوقي
rows.claim: Al-Marzūqī pairs night with day and the night with the daytime period.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام المرزوقي : الليل بإزاء النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun accompanies daytime and the moon nighttime; both are creatures subjected to God’s command.
rows.anchor: والشمس} : المشتمل عليها النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their alternation and subjection serve creatures’ needs and plainly demonstrate God’s existence, oneness, knowledge, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: تعاقب الليل والنهار على الوجه الذي يتفرع عليه منافع الخلق ومصالحهم وتذلل الشمس والقمر لما يراد منهما من أظهر العلامات الدالة على وجوده تعالى ووحدانيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs invite the seeker to look now with the heart’s eye at God’s workmanship, including the revival of the earth and the lengthening of the shade, in hope of seeing Him by His grace in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: امروز از صنع من بامن نكر بديده دل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not prostrate to the sun or moon because they are created beings subjected to commands just as humans are.
rows.anchor: لأنهما من جملة مخلوقاته المسخرة لأوامره مثلكم

rows.speaker: أهل الظاهر
rows.claim: For outward interpreters, the command is creational rather than a legal command, since the sun and moon lack knowledge and choice.
rows.anchor: والمراد : الأمر التكويني لا التكليفي إذ لا علم لهما ولا اختيار عند أهل الظاهر

rows.speaker: أهل الحقيقة
rows.claim: For the people of spiritual reality the matter is otherwise: all creation is obedient, so fairness requires the human seeker to obey as well, as Saʿdī’s verse says.
rows.anchor: وأما عند أهل الحقيقة ، فالأمر بخلافه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هن refers to the four signs; the non-rational plural takes a feminine singular pronoun, or the pronoun may refer to the feminine noun ‘signs’.
rows.anchor: الضمير للأربعة ؛ لأن حكم جماعة ما لا يعقل حكم الأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling all four signs created things, even though the sun and moon alone suffice as examples, emphasizes their complete dependence and their inability to merit worship.
rows.anchor: وتعليق الفعل بالكل مع كفاية بيان مخلوقية الشمس والقمر للإيذان بكمال سقوطهما عن رتبة المسجودية

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawī says the sun is God’s servant that cooks for people, so calling it God is foolish; it cannot remedy its own darkness or serve as a refuge when it disappears at night.
rows.anchor: وفي المثنوي : آفتاب ازامر حق طباخ ماست ابلهى باشدكه كوييم او خداست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they worship God alone, they must not prostrate to anyone else; prostration is the highest form of worship and belongs exclusively to Him.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم تعبدون إياه لا تسجدوا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some may have worshipped the sun and moon like the star-worshipping Sabians while claiming to intend worship through them; the verse forbids this mediation and commands worship of their Creator alone.
rows.anchor: كالصابئين في عبادتهم الكواكب ويزعمون أنهم يقصدون بالسجود لهما السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun cannot be made the prayer direction because its radiance, stature, and benefits could make some people mistake prostration toward it for worship of it; a designated stone direction is less suggestive of divinity.
rows.anchor: لأنها جوهر مشرق عظيم الرفعة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reports that at sunset the sun enters a sea beneath the Throne, glorifies God, and asks not to rise because people worship it; God tells it to rise, and Hell is led against the idolaters by thirteen thousand angels.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة قال : إن الشمس إذا غربت دخلت بحرا تحت العرش

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says faith in the Prophet’s community is firm even if deeds are shown off, and that placing one’s forehead in prostration to God frees a person from pride; Bursevī gives no grading.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "ليس في أمتي رياء إن راءوا فبالأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject is God and the relative pronoun is the object, with an omitted noun: God answers the supplication of the faithful who do good.
rows.anchor: الفاعل ضمير اسم الله والموصول مفعول به على إضمار المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers the righteous when they pray and rewards their obedience in the afterlife; calling that reward an answer is figurative because obedience resembles a request for its resulting reward.
rows.anchor: يعني : يعطيهم الثواب في الآخرة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet calls praise the best supplication, since praise resembles a prayer in seeking what follows from it.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : "أفضل الدعاء الحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate parse is ‘God answers them,’ with the preposition ل omitted, as in ‘when they weighed for them’ at 83:3.
rows.anchor: فحذف اللام ، كما في قوله

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī prefers supplying the omitted noun, since this is a regular construction, unlike deleting the preposition.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : الأظهر حمل الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بسط الرزق means making provision abundant and expansive.
rows.anchor: {ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده} ، لو وسعه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بغى may mean transgressing and disobeying, oppressing one another, or pride as a metonym for corruption; wealth commonly brings insolence and arrogance.
rows.anchor: لطغوا في الأرض وعصوا ، فمن العصمة أن لا تجد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains their transgression as seeking ever higher status, a better mount, and finer clothing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : بغيهم في الأرض طلبهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say that if God provided without requiring work, people would have leisure for corruption; keeping them occupied with earning prevents that, as the verse of poetry says youth, leisure, and wealth ruin a person.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لو أن الله تعالى رزق العباد من غير كسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abundant provision usually increases transgression, though a poor person can also be arrogant and unjust; poverty more often humbles, while wealth more often provokes rebellion, so universal abundance would make corruption prevail.
rows.anchor: لأن الفقر مؤد إلى الانكسار والتواضع غالبا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī says the rule is general, not universal: ʿUthmān was among the wealthiest people without visible transgression; worldly wealth is like rain that yields different growth from different soils.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (واين در غالبست

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī explains that most people lean toward desire and animal or predatory traits; wealth is a powerful cause, so greatly expanding provision would make most people transgress, as Pharaoh, Hāmān, and Qārūn illustrate.
rows.anchor: وكفى بحال فرعون وهامان وقارون ونحوهم عبرة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying states that the thing most feared for the community is worldly abundance and its flowering; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "إن أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي

rows.speaker: الصائب
rows.claim: Al-Ṣāʾib’s poem warns against indulging the soul with worldly comforts: bread and water and satiation make the laborer idle.
rows.anchor:
قال الصائب :
نفس رابد خوبناز ونعمت دنيا مكن
